reply_text:
Agents resumed; now restarting the watcher and park so this doesn't stall again.㊥ ("no affiliated codex workers active") You're right. Since about 00:30 UTC, roughly two and a half hours, no Codex agent was working on this, and that was my mistake. On the turn where I merged A+B, I didn't restart the watcher that wakes me when an agent's run finishes. So eight runs finished with nobody resuming their agents. I've now resumed all eight and restarted the watcher (`bg-…678`, park `park-3eec3964`).

㊢ (what happened) Each Codex agent hands its long run to a background job and ends its own turn. A watcher wakes me when the job exits, and I resume the agent. On every wake, my turn must end by restarting the watcher. On the A+B merge turn I did the merge and skipped that step. After that, every background job finished, but no wake came. The machine's load average has dropped to 5.7, which fits.

㊢ (resumed now) codex-17 host parsers, codex-25 `nomatch` (then `epsilonInfo`), codex-28 `let` binding, codex-29 def result type, codex-4 (then the Rob merge), codex-18 macro scopes, codex-19 `atEnd`, and codex-24 with the four completed lanes of the row-1 map. codex-27 is idle on purpose, waiting for a stop from that map. Voxterm should show them active again within a minute or two.

㊬ (integration check) It finished during the stall. At cand-1 `e251cb68`, with all six fixes merged, `ParserFn.run`, `pushSyntax` and `Array.extract` all match Lean cold. `List.foldlM` stops at shape C, as expected. So the merges together didn't break anything.

㊟ (keeping it from recurring) I've added a rule to the wake payload: every turn that wakes on the watcher ends by resuming agents and restarting the watcher, even when it also merges. On this kind of stall, the watcher's absence is what to check first.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: ("one of the high priority rows and its dependencies at a time") Agreed, and I've started. Row 1 is `Lean.Parser.mkInputContext`, the first thing `testParseModule` calls when parsing a blank file. Most of what's in flight is already on its dependency path. So the switch mainly means holding work that isn't on that path, and running one cold acceptance for the whole row instead of one per fix.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(row 1 and its dependencies) Lean's source and the curriculum list give `mkInputContext` these dependencies: `FileMap.ofString`, `toPosition` (and its `loop` and `toColumn`), `ofPosition`, `String.crlfToLf` (and its `go`), `Slice.Pos.nextn`, `Slice.pos!` and `Array.back!`. Fixes already on that path:
- `let endPos'` binding (codex-28), on `mkInputContext` itself.
- macro scopes for the `let_mvar` clash (codex-18), on `crlfToLf` and `toPosition`.
- defs without a result type, plus `binrel` (codex-29), on `nextn` and `toPosition`.
- Prop-to-Bool via `decide` (codex-19), on `toPosition`'s `&&`. The same fix applies to `atEnd`.
- numerals (codex-19) and host parsers (codex-17), on `ofPosition`.
- Already merged tonight: optParam and field notation.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(redirected)
- **codex-24:** shape C is on hold. It now maps row 1: a warm probe of every dependency at cand-1 `e251cb68`, run 4 at a time, giving one table with each dependency's first stop and which fix covers it, or "NEW" (job `invoke-1791165674973-32454-0547f558`). That tells us how far row 1 actually is from done.
- **codex-27:** off-path. It finishes its current run, commits, writes a status note, and gets an unowned row-1 stop from the map.
- **codex-25, codex-23:** codex-25 finishes `nomatch` and then closes `epsilonInfo`. codex-23's capture tool continues. Neither competes with row 1 for anything except machine time.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(how it should speed up)
1. **One cold acceptance per row:** each fix merges into a row-1 branch once it passes warm on its own target, then the row gets one cold acceptance (`mkInputContext`, its dependencies, the controls). That replaces one cold acceptance per fix. Cold runs are the slowest thing now: 66 minutes for one control in the integration check.
2. **A lighter machine:** fewer cold runs at once should bring that back towards 25 minutes per row.
3. **New packets only for row-1 stops.** When `mkInputContext` matches Lean, row 2 is the next constant `testParseModule` reaches, which is `parseHeader`.
